title: Attention - which words look at which

questions.prompt: Why does attention divide the query-key scores by sqrt(d_k) before the softmax?
options: To make the scores fit in a 32-bit float
Because a dot product of d_k-dimensional vectors grows with dimension, so without the division the softmax saturates into a nearly one-hot distribution whose gradient is nearly zero
To convert the scores into probabilities before the softmax normalises them
To make sure that every row of the weight matrix sums to exactly 1
questions.explain: The dot product of two random vectors grows roughly like sqrt(d_k), so the scores get large, and softmax of widely-spread scores is nearly one-hot - which is flat, so the gradient nearly vanishes and the model learns nothing from that step. Dividing by sqrt(d_k) keeps the scores in a range where softmax still has slope. The tempting wrong answer is the third one: softmax is what turns scores into probabilities, and the division happens before it, on raw scores.

questions.prompt: In scaled dot-product attention, what is the softmax applied to?
options: The vector of values V, to mix them
Each ROW of the scaled score matrix, so each row becomes a distribution over the tokens
Each COLUMN of the score matrix, so each column becomes a distribution
The output of the whole attention layer, to normalise the final result
questions.explain: Row i of the score matrix holds token i's scores against every other token, so softmaxing row-wise turns it into 'how much attention does token i pay to each token'. The row is the distribution; a column has no independent meaning, which is why the file's self-check asserts that every ROW sums to 1. The tempting wrong answer is the column one, and it is the mistake people make when they first see the matrix printed.

questions.prompt: Which of the three vectors decides WHAT gets carried from one token to another, and which decides WHO looks at WHOM?
options: The value carries the content and is mixed by the weights; the query and key together decide who looks at whom
The query carries the content and is mixed directly; the key and value only decide who looks at whom
All three do the same job, and they are interchangeable
The key carries the content; the query and value decide who looks at whom
questions.explain: The weights are built from query-key dot products, so the query and key decide who looks at whom. The values are what gets mixed: step 4 computes W @ V, so each output is a weighted average of the VALUE vectors. The tempting wrong answer is the second one - the query is not carried through, it is only used to compute a score and then discarded.

questions.prompt: Why is the output of the attention layer called a CONTEXTUALISED embedding rather than just an embedding?
options: Because it has been normalised so that its components sum to 1
Because it has been quantised to a smaller precision
Because each token's output now contains information borrowed from the tokens it attended to, so the same word gets a different vector in a different sentence
Because it is the output of many attention heads combined
questions.explain: After the weighted mix, token i's vector is no longer just its own embedding - it carries what it borrowed from the tokens it attended to. That is context, and it is why the word 'bank' can mean a river edge in one sentence and money in another. The tempting wrong answer is the first one - the attention weights sum to 1, but the output vector does not.

questions.prompt: The softmax in examples/01_softmax.py and the softmax in examples/04_attention_numpy.py are the same function. What differs between them?
options: The function: one is stable and one is not
What is being softmaxed: one is a row of scores over OPTIONS, the other a row of scores over TOKENS
The scaling: attention applies 1/sqrt(d_k) and the option softmax does not
The dimension: the option softmax always runs over four options
questions.explain: Identical function, different axis. A routing probability is a softmax over the options in cases/routing.json; an attention weight is a softmax over the tokens of the ticket. The tempting wrong answer is the third one - the 1/sqrt(d_k) division is applied to the scores BEFORE the softmax in attention, but it is a separate step, not a difference in the softmax itself.
